generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

  1. Student Number of absences \(\textbf{X}\) Final grade \(\textbf{Y} \, (\%)\) \(\textbf{XY}\) \(\textbf{X}^2\) \(\textbf{Y}^2\)
    \(\textbf{A}\) \({@X[1]@}\) \({@Y[1]@}\) \({@xy[1]@}\) \({@x_sq[1]@}\) \({@y_sq[1]@}\)
    \(\textbf{B}\) \({@X[2]@}\) \({@Y[2]@}\) \({@xy[2]@}\) \({@x_sq[2]@}\) \({@y_sq[2]@}\)
    \(\textbf{C}\) \({@X[3]@}\) \({@Y[3]@}\) \({@xy[3]@}\) \({@x_sq[3]@}\) \({@y_sq[3]@}\)
    \(\textbf{D}\) \({@X[4]@}\) \({@Y[4]@}\) \({@xy[4]@}\) \({@x_sq[4]@}\) \({@y_sq[4]@}\)
    \(\textbf{E}\) \({@X[5]@}\) \({@Y[5]@}\) \({@xy[5]@}\) \({@x_sq[5]@}\) \({@y_sq[5]@}\)
    \(\textbf{F}\) \({@X[6]@}\) \({@Y[6]@}\) \({@xy[6]@}\) \({@x_sq[6]@}\) \({@y_sq[6]@}\)
    \(\textbf{G}\) \({@X[7]@}\) \({@Y[7]@}\) \({@xy[7]@}\) \({@x_sq[7]@}\) \({@y_sq[7]@}\)
    \( \sum \textbf{X} ={@sumX@}\) \( \sum \textbf{Y} ={@sumY@}\) \( \sum \textbf{XY} ={@sumXY@}\) \( \sum \textbf{X} ^2 ={@sumX2@}\) \( \sum \textbf{Y} ^2 ={@sumY2@}\)

    To compute the Pearson correlation coefficient for the given data, can use the following formula:

    \( \displaystyle r = \frac{n(\sum{xy}) - (\sum{x})(\sum{y})}{\sqrt{\left[n\sum{x^2} - (\sum{x})^2\right]\left[n\sum{y^2} - (\sum{y})^2\right]}} \)

    Where:

    • \(n\) is the number of data points (in this case, {@n@} students).
    • \(\sum{x}\) and \(\sum{y}\) are the sums of the values in the X and Y datasets, respectively.
    • \(\sum{xy}\) is the sum of the products of X and Y values.
    • \(\sum{x^2}\) and \(\sum{y^2}\) are the sums of the squares of X and Y values, respectively.

    First, from the table we have the required values:

    \( \sum \textbf{X} ={@sumX@}\)

    \( \sum \textbf{Y} ={@sumY@}\)

    \( \sum \textbf{XY} ={@sumXY@}\)

    \( \sum \textbf{X} ^2 ={@sumX2@}\)

    \( \sum \textbf{Y} ^2 ={@sumY2@}\)

    Now, plug these values into the formula:

    \( \displaystyle \begin{align} r &= \frac{n(\sum{xy}) - (\sum{x})(\sum{y})}{\sqrt{\left[n\sum{x^2} - (\sum{x})^2\right]\left[n\sum{y^2} - (\sum{y})^2\right]}} \\ &= \frac{{@n@}({@sumXY@}) - ({@sumX@})({@sumY@})}{\sqrt{\left[{@n@}({@sumX2@})- ({@sumX@})^2\right]\left[{@n@}({@sumY2@}) - ({@sumY@})^2\right]}} \\ &={@r@} \end{align} \)

  2. The Pearson correlation coefficient (\(r\)) measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables. In this case, it was used to analyze the relationship between the number of absences and the final grades of students. The value of \(r\) is approximately {@decimalplaces(r,4)@}. Here the two variables have a {@mcq_correct(ta_23)[1]@}.
